purpose: define how a business solution fits together across systems, teams and vendors, so the parts can be built and the whole works
entry_criteria: Business goals and requirements are agreed
The existing landscape is documented at least roughly
Constraints on cost, time and compliance are known
procedure: Describe the business capabilities the solution must provide and the systems and people involved.
Draw the context view: what is inside the solution, what is outside, and every external connection.
Choose the main building blocks and say which are reused, bought or built, with reasons.
Define the interfaces and data ownership between the blocks and with existing systems.
Check the design against the key requirements and constraints, and list risks and open decisions.
Record the main decisions with options considered, and review the design with stakeholders.
acceptance_criteria: Build, buy or reuse is decided with reasons
Data ownership is stated per block
Key requirements are traced to blocks

validation.check: trace five key requirements to the building blocks that satisfy them
check each interface names an owner and a data owner

failure_modes.detection: Teams assume others own a function

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A customer portal is split into identity (bought), account data (existing core system) and a new notification service (built). The context diagram shows the payment provider as an external connection with a named owner.
